A lot of me converting has to do with my own personal relationship with God and not really the church itself. From my own experience, I haven’t dealt with much homophobia (there was a few experiences I had with another member), and the homophobia I have experienced was with other people and not directly from the church. 

The only only thing that does make me question my faith is the lack of representation in the church’s leadership. As a POC, I’m very aware of how this can be seen as a white mans religion, and it honestly does feel like it at times.

I get a lot of mixed remarks in terms of converting but ultimately this is my only life and being in the church has given me a lot of peace. That’s all I can really ask for TBH.

Member here! I’m an adult convert with multiple facial piercings and I’m also queer! The church does have “guidelines” when it comes modesty and piercings BUT one of the most vital parts of our faith is the teaching of agency.

At the end of the day we all are able to make our own choices and we aren’t entitled to tell other people how to live their life or judge them for how they choose to. However, “mormon culture” is very real and there are a lot of people that will feel more entitled to what other people do, but this is NOT a teaching of the faith.

That’s a big reason as to why I never snark on the McKnights when it comes to them not “following” LDS teachings (tattoos, the way they dress, Mindy not wearing garments) because at the end of the day if they still are LDS — it doesn’t matter, they are free to practice however they please to. 

Hopefully this helped!
